title: VisualZoneR: A computational protocol for spatial transcriptomics analysis
author: Kerzel, Beretta, et al.

steps.title: Calculate differential expression per zone
steps.instruction: Compute median fold‑change (FC) for each gene in each compartmental zone, determine per‑gene minima, merge with per‑signature minima, and export the results to an Excel file.

substeps.instruction: Create a data frame of median FC per gene per zone: `crc.integrated@meta.data$Zones_unique %>% group_by(GeneID, Cluster, FC) %>% summarise(MedianMS = median(FC))`.
For each gene, obtain the minimum median FC: `min_gene %>% group_by(GeneID) %>% summarise(geneMin = min(MedianMS))`.

For each signature, compute median score and its minimum: `full_df_cor_group_genes %>% group_by(SigName, Zones, RNA_Group) %>% summarise(MedianMS = median(Sig))` then `min_sig %>% group_by(SigName) %>% summarise(SigMin = min(MedianMS))`.
Merge the signature table with its minima: `full_df_cor_group <- merge(full_df_cor_group, min_sig, by = "SigName")`.

Write the merged table (excluding the fifth column) to an Excel workbook named **Full_SignaturesMedianModScore.xlsx** in the output directory: `write.xlsx(x = list("MedianSig" = full_df_cor_group[,-5]), file = paste(out_dir, "Full_SignaturesMedianModScore.xlsx", sep = "/"))`.

steps.title: Plot median module scores (Figure 11)
steps.instruction: Generate a ggplot of median module scores across zones, coloured by RNA group, add a ribbon for the minimum score, and save as PDF.

substeps.instruction: Create the plot object: `p <- ggplot(full_df_cor_group, aes(x = Zones, y = MedianMS, color = RNA_Group, fill = RNA_Group, group = RNA_Group, ymin = SigMin, ymax = MedianMS)) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.background = element_rect(color = "black"), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) + geom_point() + geom_ribbon(position = 'identity', alpha = .1) + xlab("") + ylab("Median MScore") + facet_wrap(.~SigName, ncol = 3, scales = "free")`.
Save the figure as a PDF of width 10 cm and height 7 cm: `ggsave(filename = paste(out_dir, "Full_SignaturesMedianModScore.pdf", sep = "/"), plot = p, width = 10, height = 7)`.

steps.title: Run GSEA for each zone and treatment
steps.instruction: Perform fgsea on the list of differentially expressed genes for every compartmental zone and treatment cohort, then write the combined results.

substeps.instruction: Identify all unique cluster identifiers: `Clusters <- unique(cluster0degAll[,7])`.
Initialize an empty data frame: `TopResultAllCluster <- NULL`.
For each cluster `i` in `Clusters`:
a. Extract the statistic vector for the cluster: `df2 <- cluster0degAll[cluster0degAll[,7] == i, 2]; names(df2) <- cluster0degAll[cluster0degAll[,7] == i, 6]; df2 <- df2[order(df2)]`.
b. Run fgsea with pathway database `miDB_sig2`, minimum gene set size 7, maximum 500: `test1 <- fgsea(pathways = miDB_sig2, stats = df2, minSize = 7, maxSize = 500)`.
c. Order the results by decreasing Normalised Enrichment Score (NES): `test1 <- test1[rev(order(NES))]`.
d. Convert to data frame and keep all columns: `TopResult <- as.data.frame(test1[,])[, c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7)]`.
e. Add the cluster identifier: `TopResult$Cluster <- i`.
f. Append to the master table: `TopResultAllCluster <- rbind(TopResultAllCluster, TopResult)`.

After the loop, write the full GSEA table to `GSEA_Zones_unique_integrated.res01.txt` in the data directory: `write.table(x = TopResultAllCluster, file = paste(data_dir, "GSEA_Zones_unique_integrated.res01.txt", sep = "/"), quote = FALSE, row.names = TRUE, sep = "\t")`.

steps.title: Process GSEA results and build NES matrices
steps.instruction: Split cluster identifiers into treatment group and zone, order zones, create side‑color annotation, build per‑group NES matrices, replace non‑significant scores with 0, and write the matrices.

substeps.instruction: Separate the `Cluster` column into `Group` and `Zones`: `TopResultAllCluster$Group <- stringr::str_split_fixed(TopResultAllCluster$Cluster, "_", 2)[,1]` and `TopResultAllCluster$Zones <- stringr::str_split_fixed(TopResultAllCluster$Cluster, "_", 2)[,2]`.
Create an ordered vector of zones: `orderC <- unique(TopResultAllCluster$Zones)[order(unique(TopResultAllCluster$Zones))]`.

Define side‑color vector for heatmap annotation (repeating pattern darkred×3, red×1, darkgreen×3, green×1 three times): `SideColors <- rep(c(rep("darkred",3), rep("red",1), rep("darkgreen",3), rep("green",1)), 3)`.
Helper to set row names and drop a column: `newName <- function(dfCNES,i) { rownames(dfCNES) <- dfCNES[, i]; dfCNES <- dfCNES[, -(i)]; return(dfCNES) }`.
For each treatment `ix` in `unique(TopResultAllCluster$Group)`:
a. Subset to the group: `test <- TopResultAllCluster[TopResultAllCluster$Group == ix, ]`.
b. Remove rows with missing adjusted p‑value: `test <- test[!is.na(test$padj), ]`.
c. Keep only significant pathways (adjusted p‑value < 0.05): `test <- test[test$padj < 0.05, ]`.
d. Get the list of zones present: `AllCluster <- unique(test$Zones)` and the list of pathways: `orgerGO <- unique(test$pathway)`.
e. Initialise a data frame with pathways ordered: `dfCNES <- data.frame(pathway = orgerGO[order(orgerGO)])`.
f. For each zone `j` in `AllCluster`, extract NES values and merge:
`dfC1 <- test[test$Zones == AllCluster[j], ]; dfC1 <- data.frame(dfC1[order(dfC1$pathway), c(1,6)]); colnames(dfC1) <- c("pathway", AllCluster[j]); dfCNES <- merge(dfCNES, dfC1, by = 1, all = TRUE)`.
g. Convert pathway names to row names and drop the first column: `dfCNES <- newName(dfCNES, 1)`.
h. Remove rows with > 8 missing values: `dfCNES <- dfCNES[rowSums(is.na(dfCNES)+0) < 8, ]`.
i. Replace remaining NA with 0: `dfCNES[is.na(dfCNES)] <- 0`.
j. Convert to matrix and order columns by `orderC`: `finaldf2 <- as.matrix(dfCNES); finaldf2 <- finaldf2[, orderC]`.

k. Write the matrix to a tab‑separated file named `<Group>.uniquezones.txt` in the output directory: `nameF <- paste(ix, "uniquezones.txt", sep = "."); write.table(x = finaldf2, file = paste(out_dir, nameF, sep = "/"), quote = FALSE, row.names = TRUE, sep = "\t")`.

steps.title: Create heatmap of selected pathways (Figure 12)
steps.instruction: Select a curated list of pathways, assemble a combined NES matrix across all treatment groups, and plot a heatmap with custom colours and legend.

substeps.instruction: Define the pathways to display:

`Selected.Terms <- c("GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_TYPE_I_INTERFERON","GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_INTERFERON_GAMMA","GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_VIRUS","GOBP_POSITIVE_REGULATION_OF_CYTOKINE_PRODUCTION","GOBP_T_CELL_ACTIVATION","GOBP_ADAPTIVE_IMMUNE_RESPONSE","GOBP_REGULATION_OF_IMMUNE_EFFECTOR_PROCESS","IL10_RO","HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS","HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY","HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION","HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS","HALLMARK_PEROXISOME","GOBP_SHORT_CHAIN_FATTY_ACID_METABOLIC_PROCESS","GOBP_LIPID_OXIDATION","HALLMARK_BILE_ACID_METABOLISM")`.
Create a vector of the per‑group matrix filenames: `dfNames <- paste0(unique(TopResultAllCluster$Group), ".uniquezones.txt")`.
Initialize an empty matrix to hold combined data: `ix3 <- matrix(nrow = length(Selected.Terms), ncol = 0); row.names(ix3) <- Selected.Terms`.
For each file `i` in `dfNames`:
a. Load the group's NES matrix: `ix <- read.table(paste(out_dir, i, sep = "/"), header = TRUE, sep = "\t")`.
b. Keep only rows that are in `Selected.Terms`: `ix <- ix[rownames(ix) %in% Selected.Terms, ]`.
c. Identify any selected terms missing from the file: `diffG <- setdiff(Selected.Terms, rownames(ix))`.
d. Create a zero‑filled matrix for missing terms (8 columns assumed): `diffM <- matrix(rep(0, 8 * length(diffG)), ncol = 8); rownames(diffM) <- diffG; colnames(diffM) <- colnames(ix)`.
e. Append missing rows: `ix2 <- rbind(ix, diffM)`; reorder to match `Selected.Terms`: `ix2 <- ix2[Selected.Terms, ]`.
f. Prefix column names with the group identifier: `colnames(ix2) <- paste(sub(".uniquezones.txt", "", i), colnames(ix2), sep = ".")`.
g. Bind to the combined matrix: `ix3 <- cbind(ix3, ix2)`.
Convert the final combined object to a matrix: `ix3 <- as.matrix(ix3)`.
Open a PDF device of height 6 cm and width 8 cm: `pdf(paste(out_dir, "Heatmap.uniquezones.pdf", sep = "/"), heigh = 6, width = 8)`.
Plot the heatmap using `heatmap.2` with the following parameters:

`heatmap.2(ix3, margins = c(8, 22), col = viridisLite::viridis(10), cexCol = 1, cexRow = .8, keysize = 1.1, dendrogram = "none", colsep = c(8,16), main = i, scale = "none", Rowv = FALSE, Colv = FALSE, ColSideColors = SideColors)`.
Add a legend in the top‑right corner indicating zone colours:
`legend("topright", legend = c("Inner tumor", "Border tumor", "Peritumor", "Liver"), col = unique(SideColors), lty = 1, lwd = 5, cex = .7)`.
Close the PDF device: `dev.off()`.
